dimension_assessments.summary: The signature quantifies over Feller probability kernels and invariant probability laws on NNReal, with exactly the tightness, local convergence, and weak-limit premises. Reindexing covers a convergent subsequence.

The helper bounds each expectation by norm(f). Tightness and local uniform convergence yield compact error ≤ eps/2 and tail error < eps/2. Weak convergence applies to fixed f and Pf; invariance and finite-measure separation then give the claimed measure equality.

P z is the next-state probability law conditional on current nonnegative resources z. The conclusion is one-step stationarity of the limiting law. This generic bridge introduces no household timing, income-independence, or asset-coordinate reinterpretation.

Rendered extraction pp. 1–2 are printed pp. 384–385/original PDF pp. 394–395. Theorem 12.13 uses compactness and bounded-test limits. The contract and ledger correctly identify B01's noncompact tight-tail passage as a new proof.
All premises are explicit generic kernel and probability-law conditions. The helper adds only the same Markov and Feller hypotheses; no economic assumptions enter transitively.

Only approximating laws are assumed invariant; limiting invariance is derived. Premises are consistent, for example with constant identity kernels and a constant Dirac law, and contain no disguised closure conclusion.

B01 depends only on Mathlib and its new bounded-test helper, matching its empty economic dependency list. The diff adds imports and audits without changing accepted predecessor proofs; frozen-scope verification passes.

The domain is the full continuous, noncompact NNReal space. Arbitrary Feller probability kernels impose no finite-state, density, atom, or income-law restriction on later compact iid-income applications.

Zero is included as an ordinary kernel state. Neither proof uses rightMarginalValue, zeroRightMarginal, consumption derivatives, or boundary conversion. The mandatory distinction between the positive-state real marginal and economic ENNReal zero marginal is preserved.

Bounded continuous tests are integrable under probability measures, including composed laws; differences are explicitly integrable before splitting or subtraction. Tail and compact-mass conversions use measure_ne_top and finite ofReal bounds before toReal comparisons.

ProbabilityMeasure convergence is used through its bounded-continuous integral characterization. Kernel convergence is local uniform convergence of bounded tests. The argument asserts neither total-variation convergence nor convergence of unbounded moments.
No beta, return, consumption, household policy, compact-support bound, or moment premise appears in the theorem or helper. Only B01's assigned generic hypotheses are required.
Both new proof bodies contain ordinary derived arguments without sorry, admit, project axioms, native_decide, or unsafe bypasses. Controller no-sorry and prohibited-pattern checks also pass.
Each of the three new exports has exactly propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound in its transitive axiom record. The controller's 578-declaration union contains only those permitted axioms.

All three exports match the signature and axiom inventories. Both audit files cover every export with #check, assert_no_sorry, and #print axioms; the elaborated bind conclusion is genuine measure invariance.

The Markdown ledger matches the signature, compact/tail proof, hypotheses, and REVIEW_READY status. Global status preserves predecessor GREEN and later UNFORMALIZED entries. Generated-document checks pass.

The implementation proves the required noncompact stationarity bridge for actual Markov kernels and probability laws. It derives the varying-test limit and concludes equality of measures, supplying the intended ingredient for B02 without substituting a compact-state surrogate.

Markov mass one, family tightness, all bounded continuous tests, and full measure invariance are preserved. No uniqueness, global uniform convergence, common compact support, or stronger probability interpretation is added.
The only new exports are the expectation wrapper, its norm bound, and B01. They prove no boundary divergence or later economics. B02, B03, and Stage 09 contracts remain unformalized.

The inspected argument, source pages, exact signatures, complete export audits, and consistent ledger justify acceptance of B01. No unresolved mathematical or contract defect remains; later applications remain separate.
